thread:
ashley: Heads-up — starting ~08:14 UTC we saw a spike of 503s for hosted infer in eu-west-1 for route /v1/generate. Customers reporting timeouts and errors. gateway shows upstream exits.
kevin: I'm seeing a bunch of upstream pods in kube restarting with exit code 137 and some with 139 (segfault).
mike: Could be GPU OOM or driver panic. Any correlation with batch size or context length?
ashley: Pattern: higher QPS + a couple of long-context requests (~80k tokens) just before the surge. We have a repro trace from a customer request ID: req_2f1b.
sophie: Reposting logs from the runner that crashed:```stderr
[2026-03-16T08:14:31Z] infer-runner[pid:4512]: segfault at 0 ip 0x7f9a4c3b2bad sp 0x7ffcf1c9c740 error 4 in libattention.so[7f9a4c300000+120000]
[2026-03-16T08:14:31Z] infer-runner: dumping GPU stack, exit code 139
[2026-03-16T08:14:31Z] nvml: GPU 0 memory used 31.9GB / 32.0GB
```
kevin: nvml shows memory ~>99% on that card. Also saw a few containers with OOM-killer (137). Possibly kv-cache prefetch + very long prompt pushed memory over.
ashley: support-bot: customer-impact summary requested.
support-bot: Affected customers: 3 active hosted tenants in eu-west-1 reported 503s between 08:13–08:22 UTC. Fallback routing reduced successful requests by 40%. Priority: high.
mike: Short-term mitigation: enable per-route circuit breaker to fail fast on this model and route to a smaller variant, plus evict long-context requests from GPU prefetched queue. Can we add a temporary routing rule?
sophie: I pushed a routing override to route requests to model:r-7b-compat-quant during the window. That reduced 503s but latency increased on smaller model.
kevin: Forensic notes: core dumps attached to the runner show a crash in attention kernel when seq_len > 65k and kv-cache prefetch active. Repro locally with a synthetic request:```bash
python reproduce.py --model r-13b --seq 70000 --prefetch 
```
ashley: @kevin can you confirm whether this is limited to quantized kernels or all kernels?
kevin: Initial root cause looks like a boundary check regression in the fused attention kernel for 8-bit matmul path. Only seen when quant path enabled and sequence length crosses a threshold.
mike: Action plan (short): 1) rollback auto-quant for r-13b in eu-west-1 (done), 2) enable fallback routing for long-context requests to CPU-backed runners temporarily, 3) increase oom monitoring alert thresholds.
sophie: Rollback validated: no more segfault exits for 15m after rolling back auto-quant and evicting queued prefetch for active pods. However we still see occasional memory pressure warnings.
ashley: Support note for CS: send customers a message — root cause suspected kernel bug tied to quant path + long contexts; temporary mitigations applied (routing and rollback). ETA for permanent fix TBD.
support-bot: Suggested customer text draft attached.
kevin: Long-term fix: push a kernel boundary-check patch and add unit tests for edge seq lengths; add scheduler throttle for prefetch memory budget per GPU. I'll open PR and link here.
mike: Also need to update runbook: add step to quickly disable quant path per model, and preemptively route long-context requests to a slower but safe codepath.
ashley: Who's owning postmortem? I'll take ownership for write-up. @kevin and @mike please add repro steps and timelines.
kevin: I'll attach the minimal repro and kernel trace to the incident doc.
sophie: Noted. I'm going to keep an eye on eu-west-1 for the next 2 hours. :eyes:
ashley: Thanks — great response. Going to notify the account teams for the three impacted tenants. :thumbsup:
